analysis.title: The Commodities Feed: Metals under pressure while oil supply improves
key_insights: Brent is trading below $92/bbl after a second session of declines, as improving Middle East supply outweighs continued geopolitical risk.
Crude and fuel flows through the Strait of Hormuz rose to 9.1mb/d in 3Q26 from 5.1mb/d in 2Q26, but remain well below the 21.4mb/d of a year earlier (EIA data).
Brent's prompt spread has narrowed to about $2.40/bbl backwardation from more than $3/bbl a month ago, which points to easing near-term tightness.
Money managers cut their net long in NYMEX WTI by 14,719 lots to 70,584 lots last week, the seventh consecutive weekly decline.
ING expects improving supply availability to remain a headwind for oil. A renewed disruption to Hormuz flows is the key upside risk.
US natural gas extended its decline on recovering Appalachian production and warmer forecasts for the Midwest and Northeast. Record LNG feedgas flows to US export terminals provide some support.

Gold edged higher after its lowest close since September 2025. The sell-off was driven by persistent US inflation, higher Treasury yields, expectations of tighter Fed policy for longer and weakness in technology stocks.
ING expects gold to remain volatile near term, with US yields and the dollar as the key drivers. The Fed's October meeting minutes are the next catalyst.

Copper is near its lowest level in more than four months on weak technology stocks and soft Chinese data. The AI-related share sell-off raised concerns about copper demand from power grids and data centres.
China's domestic copper market shows tightness: near-term contracts trade at a sizeable premium to later-dated ones, with depleted inventories and constrained availability.

Aluminium's nearby market has tightened sharply. The Tom/next spread is above $115/t and spot trades more than $250/t over the three-month contract. ING expects this to support prices near term, with stronger production growth loosening the balance next year.

Chinese iron ore futures fell to their lowest level in four years at the start of the week on weak steel output, poor mill margins, high port inventories, strong shipments and the Simandou ramp-up. Seasonal restocking may give only limited support.

sector_views.rationale: Improving supply availability and a looser expected global balance are a headwind for prices, with renewed Hormuz disruption the main upside risk.
Low exchange inventories and prompt tightness should support prices near term, but stronger production growth loosens the balance next year.
